title: Unplayable pianos and the West End Casino summer
summary: At a New Jersey summer job the piano was unplayable, so Boyd gave him the summer off with pay.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Just to put it on-- I'm not sure anyone will ever remember to say this. All of us old time jazz people--I say in quotes--hate the development of rock and roll, with the loud guitars and all that garbage, but something--two things good have come out of the whole movement for jazz people--I'm setting it up for George.

Back in the old days, very few bass players could afford a decent instrument, so we didn't have musical basses, we had sort of thump basses, and if I recall, the term was bad note bass player--do you remember that term?
The bass player didn't have a good enough instrument, but they had notes on that they would hammer--that's what a bass player was.
And then once in a while good players would have good instruments and it would sound really musical, but out in

Carbondale, Illinois it was thump, thump, thump. The same was true with pianos. A Rhodes maybe isn't the most musical thing in the world, but at least all the notes worked. And for the record, talk about the days when a piano didn't work.

This happened to me, in particular with the Raeburn band--I don't remember the year--it was in the early days of the band, probably--I would take a guess and say 1945-- this was In New Jersey and it was a place called the West End Casino and we had the job there for the summer, we all lived in nearby roominghouses. This is the time that I babysat for Bruce Raeburn, Bruce and Susan--
(Side B of Tape 5 ended at this point. Transcript will continue in accordance with Tape 6.)
The West End Casino has a piano that was unplayable, it was an old, old, ancient broken down, ivoryless, there were keys missing. It was a piano that was impossible

to be played upon at all.
I said to Boyd, Boyd, I can't play this piano, it doesn't play, no sounds are going to come out of it, can you get the management to replace the piano, and he said I'll see what I can do.

He came back and he said they won't do anything, that's their piano. I told Boyd I couldn't play it and I wasn't going to be an idiot and sit at that thing and make believe I was playing all night. I said you can't ask me to do that for the summer, it isn't right. He said I wouldn't think of asking you to do that, you have the summer off with pay.
So I used to go with them to work and hang out, listen to them play or go out swimming in the pool if it was warm at night; that's the way I worked that summer.
Right; they knew about it. They were that stubborn and that stupid.
